narrative_purpose: Shows that the first colonists of bare volcanic ground arrive in cracks rather than on open rock, because a crack holds the moisture, shade and dust that raw tephra cannot - the physical reason succession starts where it starts.
subject: A close view of dark rough volcanic rock filling most of the frame, its surface loose with grey ash and small angular fragments. A single narrow crack runs diagonally across it. Inside and along the crack, a thin crust of pale growth spreads in patches, and from one point in the crack a single small frond rises, barely taller than the surrounding rubble, its blade divided into fine segments. On the open rock away from the crack there is nothing growing at all - only bare grey grit.
scene: A bare volcanic plain under a dim ashen sky, the plain stretching away flat and featureless into haze behind, one distant vent silhouette barely visible at the horizon.
camera: A very close low view almost at ground level, the crack running from lower left toward upper right, the horizon compressed into a thin band at the top of the frame.
light: Flat dim overcast light with no strong source, plus a faint living-teal self-glow from the pale crust and the frond so the only living thing in the frame is the only thing glowing; deep indigo in the crack's shadow.
palette: Stone grey and void-indigo dominating the rock and sky, one small area of living-teal in the crust and frond, no warm accent anywhere.
style: Painterly naturalist plate, hand-painted texture, restrained and bleak.
detail_level: Crisp on the crack, the crust and the single frond; the open rock deliberately plain and empty; the far plain and vent dissolving into haze.
composition: Rock filling the lower four fifths with the crack as the only diagonal, the small growth positioned just off centre, large areas of empty grey rock left bare on both sides for later callouts.
consistency_notes: Cool Pandora palette drained almost to grey, with the single patch of living-teal as the only life in the frame. Nothing lush may appear - the emptiness of the surrounding rock is the point, and any additional vegetation destroys the reading.
